people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Empty Mountain academy at midday on the Thanh Loan hills, walking a quiet deer path with a pale deer at his side, listening to a mountain in which no one is seen.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the scholar who founded the academy of the Empty Mountain, standing on a deer path in the hills at the hour when the mist thins, a pale deer at his side. Face: a long, calm, scholarly face with high cheekbones, a straight nose, a neat grey-black beard and moustache, deep unhurried eyes that look past the viewer into the trees; a small smile of someone who listens more than speaks. Hair: black with silver at the temples, gathered high under a scholar's cap of black gauze with a single white jade pin. Body: tall and slender, narrow-shouldered, the upright patient bearing of a man who has sat many years over books and still walks the hills daily. Clothing: the richest house robes of Không Sơn Viện: three layers of undyed mist-white silk shading to ink-grey at the hems, as though the mountain faded into cloud, the crossed collars edged in a hair-thin line of dark ink-green, borders of sparse bamboo leaves in grey thread on pale grey brocade at the sleeves, a flat white jade disc hanging from a grey silk sash. Hands and objects: the right hand lifts a slim bamboo staff with a jade knob; the left hand lies open toward the deer's muzzle; at his belt a small reed flute in a grey silk case. Background: grey hills fading into layered mist, thin pines, an empty stone pavilion far behind with its doors open, no other figure anywhere. Light: soft pale spirit-light from above and behind, a silver-white rim on his shoulders and the deer's back, dew glittering on the grass. Power: a few motes of pale grey-green light drift from his sleeves like falling mist, thin and calm, the quiet strength of a Nguyên Anh master. Expression: serene attention, a gentle half-smile, the mild face of a man for whom silence is a kind of speech. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint grey-green and cream tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last master of the Empty Mountain in the unlocked academy at dusk, sitting on the steps with his whisk across his knees and his only student asleep in the doorway behind him, the hills already given away.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the old last master of the academy of the Empty Mountain, sitting alone on the worn stone steps of the open academy at dusk, his only student asleep in the doorway behind him. Face: a thin, calm, very old face with sunken cheeks, a long straight nose, white wisps of brow and a short white beard, pale eyes clouded with age yet clear, the face of a man who has finished giving things away. Hair: long and white, loosely tied with a grey ribbon, a bare wooden pin through the knot. Body: slight and gaunt, folded small on the step, shoulders rounded, bony hands, a stillness near to the stone he sits on. Clothing: mist-white silk robes of Không Sơn Viện in three thin layers shading to ink-grey at the hems, collars edged in a hair-thin line of ink-green, grey bamboo-leaf borders on the sleeves, a white jade disc on a grey sash; the silk is soft and old, clean and very plain, for a master who kept no ornament. Hands and objects: across his knees a white horsehair whisk with a pale wooden handle; one hand rests on it, the other holds a small folded paper unread; behind him a boy of ten sleeps in the open doorway wrapped in a grey cloak. Background: a quiet academy courtyard of pale stone, a gate left wide open, bookshelf rooms dark beyond, the whole hill blue with evening and mist. Light: soft blue dusk and silver spirit-light spilling from the open door onto the steps, a gentle white rim light on his head. Power: a faint pale-grey glow gathers round the whisk's hairs, thin as breath, the last light of a Nguyên Anh cultivator at rest. Expression: peaceful and unburdened, a tired half-smile, eyes on the dark hills as if listening to someone not yet there. The whole picture is soft and faded like an old silk painting, edges darkened to brown. A faint cool grey-blue and cream tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Gate That Opens the Thunder on Kinh Trập Sơn in early spring, beating a drum of thunder-struck wood while the first rumble rolls over the sleeping valley.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Khải Lôi Môn, beating a great drum of thunder-struck wood on a high mountain ledge in early spring as the first thunder rolls below him. Face: a broad, strong, weathered face with a heavy jaw, a short black beard with a few grey hairs, bright dark eyes lifted to the clouds, a wide mouth open in a shout of joy or invitation. Hair: black, thick, tied up high in a bronze ring, loose strands whipped by the wind. Body: broad-chested, heavy-shouldered and tall, braced with feet apart, the stance of a man giving the whole body to a drumbeat. Clothing: the richest robes of Khải Lôi Môn: layered silk in storm indigo and deep slate, an outer gauze of dark blue edged with bronze-gold thunder-scroll embroidery, the crossed collars bordered in gold lightning-knots, a thick bronze-gold brocade sash with a small gold thunder-knot clasp, the wide sleeves bound back at the elbows with indigo cords; every member of the Gate wears this indigo and bronze. Hands and objects: both fists grip drumsticks of pale split wood and strike a huge drum whose skin is stretched tight on a body of black, lightning-scorched timber; its ribs are bound with bronze studs. Background: a rocky mountain ledge above a valley still brown with winter, new green only at the lowest slopes, heavy purple storm clouds piled behind, a rim of rain on the far hills. Light: pale blue-white spirit-light running along the sticks and the drum, cold violet storm light from behind, a silver rim light on his shoulders. Power: thin forks of white lightning crawl along the drum's rim and up his forearms, bright but small, the thunder power of a Nguyên Anh founder. Expression: fierce and joyful, teeth bared in a laugh, eyes shining, an invitation to the lightning. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint indigo and warm bronze tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the Gate That Opens the Thunder on the peak of Kinh Trập Sơn at the hour of his tribulation, arms lowered and eyes open, the sealed mountain behind him and the first bolt coming down.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Khải Lôi Môn, standing on the bare summit of Kinh Trập Sơn at the moment of his own tribulation, looking straight up as the first bolt descends. Face: a lean, proud, hollow-cheeked face with a long straight nose, a thin black moustache, strong brows drawn together, eyes wide and unafraid, the face of someone who has hidden a secret in a mountain. Hair: black, long, unbound and lifted by the storm wind, a bronze ring at the nape. Body: tall and spare, shoulders squared, arms slightly open at his sides, boots planted on bare rock, utterly still. Clothing: the robes of Khải Lôi Môn in storm indigo and deep slate silk, three layers with an outer gauze edged in bronze-gold thunder-scrolls, gold lightning-knots at the collars, a bronze-gold brocade sash with a thunder-knot clasp, wide sleeves lifted by the wind; the head's richest cut, now streaming and scorched at the cuffs with pale ash. Hands and objects: the right hand holds a short black iron rod with a bronze cap pointed up, the left hangs open; at his sash a small bronze key on a cord. Background: a bare grey summit, black storm clouds boiling above, the far plain lit in thin bars of cold gold, a faint seam in the mountain behind him where something was sealed. Light: a violent white-blue flash from above lighting his face and the underside of the clouds, hard violet shadow, a thin silver rim on his hair. Power: a Nguyên Anh cultivator's thunder gathers round him, white lightning running along his sleeves and the rod, the whole sky answering. Expression: stern acceptance, jaw set, eyes unflinching, no plea in it. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened and cracked. A faint cold violet tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Palace of the Nine Shao on a ridge of Thê Ngô Lĩnh at dawn, lifting her nine-piped flute to her lips as the first phoenix-coloured light touches the pipes.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Cửu Thiều Cung standing on a high ridge at dawn and raising the nine-piped flute she carved, ready to play the first of the nine tunes. Face: a serene, oval, youthful face with high smooth cheekbones, long phoenix-shaped eyes lidded in pale gold, fine straight brows, a small calm mouth; no sign of her two hundred and fifty years. Hair: glossy black, piled in a tall phoenix coil crowned with a gold phoenix-feather diadem set with green jade, two long hanging gold strings over each ear, a few fine strands drifting. Body: slender and graceful, standing straight with her elbows lifted, the poised stillness of a musician before the first note. Clothing: the richest robes of Cửu Thiều Cung: five layers of ivory and celadon-green silk, a long over-robe of pale celadon gauze worked with gold phoenix feathers, crossed collars edged in gold, borders of nine small embroidered pipes in rising lengths, a wide sash of pale gold brocade hung with nine tiny jade pipes on silk threads that chime softly; ivory and celadon with gold are the colours of the whole palace. Hands and objects: both hands lift a pipe of nine slender bamboo tubes of rising length bound with gold thread, the lips just touching the shortest; long fingers pale as jade. Background: a pale ridge of green hills with old paulownia trees, rolling clouds below, the first red-gold rim of the sun, a single pale bird high in the haze. Light: dawn spirit-light flooding from the right, warm gold on the pipes and her cheek, a soft celadon glow in her gauze, rim light along her hair. Power: gold and green motes of sound rise from the pipes like drifting feathers and thin glowing rings, a Nguyên Anh master's grace. Expression: absorbed, composed and luminous, eyes half closed, the quiet confidence of someone whose music can call a phoenix. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint jade-green and amber tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the Palace of the Nine Shao on the steps of her ruined gate at the end of the War of the Nine Shao, playing the last tune on a long pipe as the army closes in below.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Cửu Thiều Cung standing on the broken steps of her palace gate, playing the last of the nine tunes on a long pipe as an army gathers below. Face: a stately, resolute face with a high forehead, strong delicate nose, long lidded eyes shadowed by weariness, a firm mouth; soot on one cheekbone and a bruise-pale pallor. Hair: black, once coiled high in a phoenix crown, now half fallen and caught by the wind, one gold phoenix-feather diadem tilted, a green jade pin still holding a lock. Body: tall and slim in an upright stance, feet apart on the steps, shoulders thrown back, a trembling fatigue under the straight line. Clothing: the richest robes of Cửu Thiều Cung: layers of ivory and celadon-green silk with a long over-robe of celadon gauze worked with gold phoenix feathers, crossed collars edged in gold, borders of nine tiny pipes, now singed brown at the sleeves and dusted with ash, a gold brocade sash with nine small jade pipes still chiming on their threads. Hands and objects: both hands hold a long pipe of bamboo bound with gold thread to her lips; at her feet lies a cracked jade drum and a fallen banner of ivory silk. Background: the gate of a pale palace half fallen, smoke curling over the hills, a dark mass of an army with a thousand small lanterns climbing the slope in the dusk. Light: a copper-red firelight from below and a cold celadon glow from her gauze, with a thin gold rim on her profile. Power: golden rings of sound spread from the pipe through the smoke, each one pushing back a little of the dark, the final strength of a Nguyên Anh master. Expression: calm and unyielding, wet-eyed but steady, as though the last tune were the only answer worth giving. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened and soft with soot. A faint ash-grey and ember tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the School of the Northern Sky on the ice of Ngọc Hồ Sơn, her ice sword Phi Tuyết planted in a drift, a reed pipe at her lips, snow falling in the eighth month while the fire mountain glows behind.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Hồ Thiên Phái standing on a frozen lake at night with her ice sword stuck point-down in a snowdrift, playing a reed pipe as snow falls and a fire mountain glows far behind. Face: a strong, high-cheeked northern face with wind-reddened skin, narrow dark eyes, a fine straight nose, full lips around a reed pipe, a thin silver scar on the chin. Hair: black with grey streaks, in many thin braids caught in a silver circlet set with pale blue stones, a few braids over her shoulder. Body: broad-shouldered and tall, braced against the wind, the sturdy stance of a rider of the far north. Clothing: the richest house robes of Hồ Thiên Phái: layers of ice-blue and night-indigo silk with a snow-white fur trim at collar and cuff, a wide over-robe of pale blue brocade embroidered with silver reed-pipe and falling-snow motifs, a nomad-style crossed collar edged in silver, a deep indigo sash with a silver clasp shaped like a star; these colours mark the whole school. Hands and objects: the left hand holds a long reed pipe to her lips; the right rests on the pommel of the sword Phi Tuyết, a blade of clear ice that never melts, glinting pale blue; a smaller reed pipe hangs at her belt. Background: a frozen lake under a black sky full of stars, snow falling in thick flakes, a far cone of red fire glowing under the ice and steam on the horizon. Light: a cold silver-blue glow from the ice sword and the snow, a warm orange rim light from the distant volcano on one side of her face and shoulder. Power: pale blue frost-qi spirals up the blade and falls as glittering motes, a Kết Đan master of ice beside a mountain of fire. Expression: proud, wild and calm, eyes half closed on the music, the look of one who lives at the edge of the cold. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint ice-blue and ember tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Gate of the Red Wall at dawn among the red cliffs of Đan Huyệt Châu, standing in a vent's warm breath as the rock glows like a rosy cloud.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Xích Thành Môn standing at dawn on a red cliff above a steaming vent, the rock glowing round him like a rosy cloud. Face: a warm, open, handsome face with a broad forehead, a straight nose, bright amber eyes, a short neat reddish-brown beard and a generous, easy smile. Hair: auburn, tied up in a high knot with a gold crown shaped like a flame, a few strands lifted by the rising heat. Body: strong and broad, standing at ease with the chest open, a bearing of simple pride. Clothing: the richest robes of Xích Thành Môn: layered silk in rose-pink and vermilion with cream inner collars, an outer gauze of soft coral, crossed collars bordered in gold flame-scrolls, wide sleeves embroidered with cliff-and-cloud patterns in gold thread, a black basalt-coloured sash with a flame-shaped gold clasp; the whole Gate wears rose and vermilion with gold flame borders. Hands and objects: the right hand cups a small living flame as one cups a bird; the left lifts a gold rod crowned with a red stone; at his hip a small bronze incense burner on a chain. Background: tall red cliffs with plumes of white steam rising from vents, a pale pink dawn sky and a few long clouds in rose and gold, a stairway cut into the rock far below. Light: warm rose-gold dawn light from the left and a soft ember glow from the flame on his chin and sleeves, gentle rim light on his hair. Power: warm orange and rose motes of fire rise round him like drifting petals, soft and large, a Nguyên Anh master's calm heat. Expression: warm, confident and kindly, laughing eyes, a man pleased by the world he made. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint rose and gold tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the Gate of the Red Wall in his hall at night with the fire arts blazing in a brazier at his feet and the glow of a burning village in the doorway behind him.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Xích Thành Môn standing in a dark hall before a roaring brazier, the red glow of a distant burning village in the doorway behind him. Face: a hard, gaunt, handsome face with high cheekbones, a hooked nose, narrow gold-brown eyes, a thin cruel mouth, a short pointed black beard, skin shining in the heat. Hair: black with a streak of red, bound up in a tall dark crown of black iron shaped like flames, a few loose strands across the forehead. Body: tall, lean and straight, shoulders squared, a hunger in the stillness. Clothing: the richest robes of Xích Thành Môn turned dark: heavy layers of crimson and vermilion silk with a black over-robe, the crossed collars bordered in gold flame-scrolls, the rose of the founder's days burned to deep red, the sleeves embroidered with a gold cliff-and-flame pattern, a black basalt sash with a flame-shaped gold clasp; the hems are dusted with soot. Hands and objects: both palms are held over the brazier, from which tongues of fire rise obediently into his hands; on a low table a red stone rod and a smoking incense bowl. Background: a tall dark hall with red lacquered pillars, an open doorway giving on a night sky stained orange by a burning village, ash drifting in. Light: hard orange firelight from below throwing his shadow high on the pillars and carving his cheekbones, a thin red rim light along his shoulders. Power: flames coil round his arms like willing snakes, deep red and orange, a Kết Đan cultivator who feeds on fire and gives it freely. Expression: cold, absorbed and proud, eyes fixed on the fire, a quiet appetite in the face. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened and smoked. A faint crimson and soot-brown tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Gate of the Cold River in a straw cloak and hat on a skiff in a snowing river, fishing alone on the ice-edge at dusk, and the river empty to every shore.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Hàn Giang Môn in a small skiff on a snowing river, fishing alone at dusk with the far banks lost in white. Face: a long, weathered, patient face half hidden under a hat brim, a thin grey beard iced at the tips, deep-set pale eyes, a fisherman's calm lines at the mouth. Hair: grey-white, long, tied low at the nape with a slate-blue cord, a pale jade ring in the knot. Body: lean and narrow, seated upright at the stern of the skiff, shoulders hung with snow, the patience of a man who can wait for a month. Clothing: the richest robes of Hàn Giang Môn: soft layers of slate-blue and frost-white silk, over them a layered cape of silver-grey silk fringe cut like a straw cloak, each strand glittering with frost, crossed collars edged in white, borders of cold ripple waves in blue thread, a plain sash with a pale jade fish pendant, and a wide conical hat of woven pale reed with a sheer grey veil to the shoulders. Hands and objects: both hands hold a long bamboo fishing rod whose thread falls into a dark gap in the ice; beside him a small wicker basket with one silver fish and a thin lantern of grey paper. Background: a wide frozen river lost in falling snow, grey cliffs fading in mist, a single far boat light, the skiff leaving a dark wake in the glassy water. Light: cold silver-blue light of a snow dusk from all sides, a soft white glow on the frost of the cape, a faint warm lantern glimmer on his hands. Power: pale blue frost-qi curls along the line and the water, a few ice motes drifting, a Kết Đan cultivator's quiet cold. Expression: serene, solitary and contented, a still gaze on the water, no wish to be anywhere else. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint slate-blue and white tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the Gate of the Cold River alone on a skiff at the river mouth at night, the lantern-fleet of the enemy behind him, the sword out and the oars shipped, the cloak frosted white.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Hàn Giang Môn standing in a lone skiff on the frozen river mouth at night, sword drawn, the lights of an enemy fleet ranked behind him. Face: a stern, narrow, handsome face with high cheekbones, a firm jaw clean-shaven, grey-blue eyes narrowed against the wind, a mouth held tight, hoar frost on the brows. Hair: black, long and tied up at the crown with a slate-blue cord and a pale jade ring, a long tail whipping in the wind. Body: tall and lean, square-shouldered in the boat, knees slightly bent for balance, a fighter's quiet readiness. Clothing: the robes of Hàn Giang Môn in slate-blue and frost-white silk, a layered cape of silver-grey silk fringe cut like a straw cloak glittering with ice, crossed collars edged in white with cold ripple borders in blue thread, a pale jade fish on a plain sash, a reed hat flung back on its cord between his shoulders; the head's richest cut, a little scorched along one sleeve. Hands and objects: his right hand holds a straight narrow sword whose blade shines pale blue; the left holds a lantern of grey paper; a single oar lies shipped along the gunwale. Background: a dark frozen river mouth, black water and plates of ice, a row of enemy lanterns glittering in the distance, snow driven sideways, cliffs at either side. Light: cold blue-silver light from the blade and the ice, a faint warm lantern glow on his chin, a thin white rim light along his shoulders. Power: frost-qi spreads from the blade onto the water in widening white rings, a Kết Đan cultivator's last stand. Expression: grim, clear and resolute, eyes on the enemy lights, no fear in the face. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint cold blue and silver tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Pavilion of the Lone Sail at the end of the jetty on Cô Vụ Đảo, watching the last ship leave the bay with the silver needle that always points to it held up before him, the sea blue to the sky.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Cô Phàm Các at the end of a stone jetty on a misty island, holding up his silver needle that points to the last ship leaving the bay. Face: a calm, weathered, sun-dark face with a broad forehead, a hawk nose, a salt-and-pepper beard, narrow sea-grey eyes screwed against the glare, laugh lines at the corners. Hair: black and grey, tied up in a topknot with a sea-blue ribbon and a silver pin, a few strands blown across the cheek. Body: tall, sturdy and balanced, legs apart as if on a deck, shoulders wide, the easy poise of a sailor who reads water like a scripture. Clothing: the richest robes of Cô Phàm Các: layers of deep sea-blue silk with an outer gauze of white sailcloth-pale silk, crossed collars bordered in silver, wide sleeves embroidered with white wave-crests and a single sail in silver thread, a navy brocade sash with a small silver compass clasp; deep blue and sail-white mark the whole Pavilion. Hands and objects: the right hand lifts a slender silver needle between two fingers, its point steady toward the horizon; the left holds a coil of blue silk rope; a brass spyglass hangs at his hip. Background: a grey stone jetty running out into a bay of sea-blue water, a single white sail growing small on the horizon, drifting sea mist, pale rocks and gulls. Light: clear pale sea-light from the front, a bright white glimmer on the needle and the waves, a soft blue rim on his hair. Power: pale blue and silver motes run along the needle toward the sail like a drawn line of light, a Kết Đan master of the sea road. Expression: peaceful, far-sighted and quietly amused, eyes on the horizon. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint sea-blue and cream tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the Pavilion of the Lone Sail at the helm of the flagship in the storm that took the whole fleet, one hand on the tiller, the other holding up the signal lantern while a line of lamps fades behind him.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Cô Phàm Các at the helm of his flagship in a great storm, holding up a signal lantern while the lights of his fleet vanish one by one behind him. Face: a lean, tanned, determined face with a square jaw, a straight nose, wet black eyebrows, narrow dark eyes that count the lanterns behind him, a mouth set hard against the spray. Hair: black, long, plastered to the neck and tied with a sea-blue cord, a silver pin at the crown. Body: tall and wiry, braced with both feet wide, knees bent against the roll of the deck. Clothing: the robes of Cô Phàm Các in deep sea-blue silk and a sailcloth-pale over-gauze streaming in the gale, crossed collars bordered in silver, wave-crest and single-sail embroidery in silver thread, a navy brocade sash with a silver compass clasp, soaked dark at the hems and clinging to his shoulders; the head's richest cut. Hands and objects: the right hand grips the wooden tiller bound in blue silk; the left holds high a glass lantern whose white flame burns steady despite the wind; a silver needle hangs on a cord at his chest, pointing astern. Background: a black sea in mountainous waves, a white-lit sky of racing cloud, the rigging of a great ship, and behind it a long line of small lanterns vanishing one after another in the spray. Light: white lightning-flash from the sky, a steady warm lantern gold on his face, silver-blue rim light along his wet shoulders. Power: pale blue qi runs along the tiller and out into the water in thin bright lines, a Kết Đan helmsman holding a fleet together to the end. Expression: fixed, steady and unbowed, eyes on the lanterns of his people. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened and streaked. A faint storm blue and silver tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the School of the Fallen Petals under the peach trees where the forest meets the bay, in the first spring rain of petals, forging the twin swords from a single branch.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Lạc Anh Phái standing among peach trees at the bay's edge in a storm of falling petals, holding up two slim swords she forged from one branch. Face: a delicate, lovely, intelligent face with a pale oval shape, a small straight nose, long dark eyes with a quiet fire, a gentle, firm mouth, peach-pink petals on her cheek. Hair: black and long, half up in a high knot with a gold peach-blossom comb, the rest falling in a waterfall down her back and carrying petals. Body: slender and straight, standing with the grace of a dancer, a swordswoman's balance. Clothing: the richest robes of Lạc Anh Phái: layers of peach-blossom pink, petal-white and deep plum silk, an outer gauze of pale pink embroidered all over with falling petals in white and rose thread, crossed collars edged in plum, borders of drifting petals, a plum brocade sash with a gold peach-blossom clasp; these three colours mark the whole School. Hands and objects: in her right hand the sword Phi Hồng, a bright blade with a faint red-gold lustre and a crimson tassel; in her left Tàn Hồng, darker, with a pale pink tassel; both blades point gently up. Background: a grove of peach trees in full bloom running down to a pale bay and a dark forest edge, petals blown like snow over sand, a light haze of spring rain. Light: soft pink-gold spring light from above left, petals glowing translucent against the sun, a gentle white rim light on her hair and sleeves. Power: pink and gold qi motes gather in the petals around the blades, a Nguyên Anh master's quiet command of a thousand springs. Expression: joyful, proud and tender, a half-smile at her own work. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint peach-pink and cream tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the last head of the School of the Fallen Petals alone on a cliff top at night with the sword Tàn Hồng, gazing at the full moon over a school that has split, the night she vanished.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the last head of Lạc Anh Phái standing alone on a cliff at night, the sword Tàn Hồng in her hand, her face turned up to a full moon over a divided school. Face: a pale, composed, sorrowful face with a long oval shape, fine straight brows, large dark eyes wet with moonlight, a soft mouth tightened in resolve. Hair: black and long, bound in a low knot with a plum ribbon and a silver moon-shaped comb, long strands blowing across her shoulder. Body: tall and slim, upright with a slight lean toward the moon, a sword-hand's relaxed grip. Clothing: the robes of Lạc Anh Phái in peach-blossom pink, petal-white and deep plum silk, an outer gauze of pale pink with a falling-petal embroidery in white and rose thread, plum-edged collars, a plum brocade sash with a gold peach-blossom clasp, a long pale veil of moon-white gauze over one shoulder; the head's richest cut, the pink gone grey-silver in the moonlight. Hands and objects: the right hand holds the dark sword Tàn Hồng point-down; the left lifts a palm to the moon as if to catch light; at her sash a small unlit paper lantern. Background: a high cliff above a black sea, a full pale moon with thin cloud across it, far below the tiny glimmers of a split school's two camps, peach petals blowing past. Light: cold silver moonlight from the upper right, a white rim on her profile and sword, a faint rose glow in her sleeves. Power: pale silver-pink qi gathers round the blade and her raised hand like moonlit petals, a Kết Đan master drawing in her breath before leaving. Expression: quiet farewell, calm eyes on the moon, a long grief behind the face. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint moon-silver and pale plum tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the sworn sister and rival in the rain forest of Tiêu Vũ Lâm under a dripping canopy, sitting by a stream with the sword Phi Hồng across her knees, waiting for an heir who has not come.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the elder of Lạc Anh Phái, sitting on a mossy rock beside a stream deep in the rain forest with the sword Phi Hồng laid across her knees, waiting. Face: a handsome, weathered, strong-boned face with a broad forehead, a firm straight nose, level dark eyes, a stubborn mouth, a few fine lines of rain-forest wind at the eyes. Hair: black and grey, braided in one thick plait over the shoulder and wound with a peach-pink ribbon, dripping with wet. Body: upright and spare, strong-shouldered, sitting very still with one foot drawn up, the watchful ease of a guard who does not sleep. Clothing: the robes of Lạc Anh Phái in peach-blossom pink, petal-white and deep plum silk, an outer gauze of deep plum with drifting petals embroidered in rose thread, plum-edged collars, a plum brocade sash with a gold peach-blossom clasp; the pink is faded to the colour of old petals and the silk beaded with rain, the elder's richer cut. Hands and objects: both hands rest on a bright sword with a faint red-gold lustre and a crimson tassel; the right thumb is on the guard; beside her a waxed paper umbrella closed and propped. Background: a dense green rain forest, huge dripping leaves and hanging vines, a narrow stream over stones, mist between great tree trunks, a light rain falling. Light: soft green-grey light filtered through the canopy, a gentle red-gold glow from the blade onto her hands and chin, a silver rim light on wet hair. Power: a thin red-gold qi trails from the blade and rises through the rain in fine threads, a Kết Đan elder who keeps her blade alive. Expression: patient, loyal and a little sad, looking down the path for a footstep that does not come. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint forest green and rose tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the pirate lord who founded the Gate That Swallows the Sea, at the last stand on his islet in the burning hold, the whale-tooth sabre Kình Nha raised and the fleet of the Purge closing on the dark water behind him.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the pirate lord who founded Thôn Hải Môn, standing in the doorway of his burning sea-hold with the sabre Kình Nha raised, the ships of the Pirate Purge closing on the water behind him. Face: a huge, hard, tanned face with a heavy jaw, a broad flattened nose, a black beard with a stripe of white, small black eyes under thick brows, a gold tooth glinting in a grin that is not quite mirth. Hair: black, oiled and tied in a thick tail with a bone ring and a deep teal band, loose strands wet with spray. Body: enormously broad and tall, shoulders like a door, thick forearms with a pale scar across one, planted like a mast. Clothing: the richest robes of Thôn Hải Môn: heavy layers of whale-black and deep teal silk, an outer gauze of grey-black with a curling whale-tail embroidered in silver across the back, crossed collars bordered in bone-white thread, silver whale-tooth ornaments at the shoulders and sash, a black brocade sash with a bone-white clasp; the whole Gate wears whale-black, teal and bone-white; the hems are scorched. Hands and objects: the right hand raises a broad curved sabre with a pale whale-tooth-white blade and a teal tassel; the left holds the sash, where a coil of rope and a small black drum hang. Background: a burning sea-hold of black timber on a rocky islet, flames and smoke climbing, a dark sea scattered with the lantern-lights of a hundred warships, stars between smoke. Light: hard orange firelight from the left on his face and chest, a cold blue-teal moonlit rim from the sea on his shoulders. Power: a Kết Đan sea-lord's dark teal qi rolls off him like a breaking wave, cold spray and foam-white motes drifting through the smoke. Expression: defiant, savage and laughing, teeth bared, a man who intends to take the sea with him. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened and smoked. A faint teal, ember and bone tint.

people.imagined: Remembered: the founder of the Gate of the Army-Breaker Star on a ridge of Dao Quang Lĩnh at dawn on the eve of the rebellion, his spear planted beside him, looking down on the camp of his lord and the camps of his own disciples.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of the founder of Phá Quân Môn standing on a mountain ridge at dawn on the eve of his rebellion, his spear planted beside him, looking down on a vast camp. Face: a lean, hawkish, hard face with a high-bridged nose, a thin dark moustache, narrow wolf-pale grey eyes, a long jaw, deep lines beside the mouth, a faint scar across the left brow. Hair: black with grey at the temples, bound back with a silver band under a tall dark crown of steel set with seven small silver stars in a Dipper curve. Body: tall, rangy and strong, broad at the shoulder and narrow at the hip, standing with his weight on one leg like a wolf at rest. Clothing: the richest robes of Phá Quân Môn: layers of steel-grey and wolf-star violet-black silk, an outer gauze of smoke grey, crossed collars bordered in silver, borders of silver seven-star Dipper curves and wolf heads, dark lacquered scale shoulder-guards and bracers over the silk, a wide black brocade sash with a silver star clasp; the whole Gate wears steel-grey, violet-black and silver. Hands and objects: the right hand rests on a long black spear with a silver wolf-head socket and a violet tassel, its point driven in the earth; the left hand is clasped behind his back. Background: a high ridge above a plain filled with the campfires of a great army, the sky paling from deep violet to pale gold, seven faint stars still visible in the west. Light: a cold violet-silver dawn light from the front, a steel-grey glimmer along the spear, a pale gold rim light from the rising sun on his shoulders. Power: violet-silver qi gathers in a pale star-shaped halo behind him and wolf-shaped wisps coil round the spear, a Nguyên Anh general's pride. Expression: commanding, cold and certain, a ruthless clarity about the face. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. A faint steel-violet and silver tint.
